reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin campus publishes 19 MW of IT load across 242,000 square feet, which makes it a compliance-focused colocation site rather than a power source for large-scale AI training.

The certifications tell the same story. PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942 are the credentials a facility needs to host regulated financial, healthcare and federal workloads. Those tenants bring steady, contracted demand and strict physical and procedural requirements. They are not the customers who sign for interruptible, high-density GPU capacity at short notice.

Within Texas the campus ranks tenth by published capacity among the 19 facilities that disclose a figure, and its 19 MW is 4 percent of the state's 475 MW of published IT load. That ranking covers a minority of supply. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, and most publish no capacity at all, so the tenth-place position describes the disclosed subset rather than the state's real inventory.

At an assumed 40 kW per rack, 19 MW is roughly 475 racks of compute, a meaningful amount and a small one next to hyperscale AI hubs. The published IT load is the ceiling. Actual availability, the power delivery headroom needed for GPU densities above legacy IT, and grid interconnection quality are not published, and the suitability score of 62 is built only from published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing from the inputs.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
